_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 4 (Magellan/MagE, Keck II/ESI echellette mode, Ohara BSL7Y prism glass)
_meta.companion: data/presets_sources.json (round 1), data/presets_sources_2.json (round 2), data/presets_sources_3.json (round 3); same structure; human-readable twin data/round4/mage_esi.md. Keys IMACS, KTG02 and OHWEB are identical copies of earlier-round files, re-saved under rawdata/presets/mage/ or esi/.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (is_derived = the value itself is derived). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). note = context or caveat. Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (whitespace/glyph-normalised).
_meta.quote_normalisation: Quotes copied from pdftotext (layout and raw) / HTML text; degree glyphs, primes, micro signs, dashes and table bars normalised; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells; a piece also passes if it matches with all whitespace removed.

mage.title: Magellan II (Clay) / MagE (Magellan Echellette: prism-cross-dispersed echellette, vacuum Schmidt camera; on Magellan I Baade per the 2017 handout and 2024 manual)
mage.recommended_preset: 1.0" x 10" slit (the slit every source quotes R for). D = 6.5 m, F = 11.0 (Magellan f/11; 2.88"/mm at the slit), 1 object, mirror collimator (off-axis paraboloid) f_col = 1094 mm -> W = 99 mm as stated (1094/11.0 = 99.45 mm DERIVED), camera: vacuum Schmidt f = 138 mm (f/1.4), echellette 175 gr/mm, delta = 32.3 deg, quasi-Littrow (theta and gamma NOT published: 0 here), orders 6-20; cross-disperser: two fused-silica prisms, 46 deg in double pass + 40 deg in single pass (three prism passes; the 'rotation angles ... adjusted to control the anamorphic beam distortion' are NOT published -> minimum deviation); detector E2V CCD42-20, 2048 (dispersion, DERIVED) x 1024 x 13.5 um. Validate against R = 4100 at 1" (design; M08, LCOMG) and the measured R = 4770 +/- 8 (1") / 2545 +/- 37 (2") from sky lines (R18); the per-order dispersion of M08 Table 2 (0.231 A/px in order 20 at 3125 A ... 0.788 A/px in order 6 at 9700 A = 22.2-24.4 km/s/px DERIVED); coverage 3100 A - 1 um in orders 6-20 with order centres ~6.2 um/m; 0.3"/px along the slit (3 px per arcsec). The central wavelength (which order sits at the detector centre) is NOT published.

alternatives.value: two large fused-silica prisms (one single-pass, one double-pass)
alternatives.quote: two large fused-silica prisms (one single-pass, one double-pass)
dispersed by the reflection grating, and is separated into echelle orders by double-pass and single-pass prisms

cross_disperser.note: fused-silica grade NOT stated (use Malitson 1965). Path order (46 deg prism before and after the grating, then the 40 deg prism) is inferred from 'first'/'second' and the ESI layout that M08 says MagE follows; no MagE source states it.

alternatives.quote: The prisms are aligned to minimize anamorphic magnification.

value.type: vacuum Schmidt (aspheric CaF2 corrector + fused-silica meniscus = dewar window; spherical mirror 200 mm dia., R = 293 mm; fused-silica field flattener)

camera.quote: is placed at the prime focus of a vacuum Schmidt camera with a focal length of 138 mm. The angular field of view of the camera is 12.7˚

alternatives.quote: An f/1.4 Schmidt camera focuses the ~100 mm collimated beam

alternatives.value: prime focus Schmidt with a doublet corrector
alternatives.quote: The camera is a prime focus Schmidt with a doublet corrector.

camera.derived: DERIVED: 138/99.45 = f/1.39; detector diagonal 30.9 mm subtends 2 atan(15.46/138) = 12.8 deg (matches the 12.7 deg field)

detector.quote: The MagE CCD is an E2V 42-20 back-illuminated device, which has a 2048x1024 format with 13.5 µm pixels.

alternatives.quote: The MagE CCD is an E2V 42-20, which has a 2048×1024 format with 13.5 micron pixels.

detector_dispersion_axis.quote: the best focus in the x (dispersion) and y (spatial) dimensions agrees to within 100 collimator units
detector_dispersion_axis.derived: DERIVED: order 6 free spectral range 9700/6 = 1617 A at 0.788 A/px (M08 Table 2) = 2052 px, so orders run along the 2048-px axis; the 15 orders are stacked along the 1024-px axis

binning.value: 1, 2, 3 or 4 in X and Y independently; default NOT FOUND
binning.quote: The Binning pulldown menu allows the observer to select pixel binning factors of 1, 2, 3, or 4 in the X and Y dimension independently.

R_1arcsec_design.quote: The grating provides a resolution of R=4100 for a 1 arcsec slit on Magellan.

alternatives.quote: The spectral resolution for a 1" slit is R~4100.
This grating gives a resolution of R=4100 for a 1 arcsec slit.

R_1arcsec_design.derived: DERIVED (geometric): 1" slit = 0.3468 mm x 138/1094 = 43.7 um = 3.24 px; Littrow 23.2 km/s/px -> FWHM 75.2 km/s -> R = 3990; with the M08 Table 2 dispersion at 5590 A (0.426 A/px): R = 4050

R_measured_sky_lines.unit: lambda/dlambda (median over the spectrum; Gaussian FWHM of night-sky lines) vs slit width (arcsec)
R_measured_sky_lines.quote: the median resolution and standard deviation are R = 2545 ± 37; the observations taken with the 100 slit have R = 4770 ± 8 . As expected for an echellete, the spectral resolution is constant with wavelength. These measured resolutions are higher than the design resolution of R ∼ 4100
R_measured_sky_lines.note: '100 slit' / '200 slit' = 1" / 2" (double prime rendered as 00). Sky lines fill the slit, so these are slit-limited values.
R_measured_sky_lines.derived: DERIVED: 4770/4100 = 1.16; geometric R for 2" = 1990 vs 2545 measured (1.28)

R_range.quote: MagE provides resolutions of R~1000 to R~8000, using a movable slit plate containing non- overlapping slits that are 10” long and 0.5” to 5” wide.

alternatives.quote: corresponding to resolutions of R ∼ 1000 (∼ 120 km s−1 ) to R ∼ 8000 (∼ 12 km s−1 )
alternatives.note: c/8000 = 37 km/s, so '~12 km/s' is inconsistent with R ~ 8000

dispersion_per_order.unit: order: [central wavelength A, dispersion A/pixel at that wavelength]

alternatives.quote: is a medium–resolution (R ≃ 4100, 22 km s−1 pixel−1 ) ... Dispersion on the chip ranges from 0.3 Å pixel−1 (blue) to 0.6 Å pixel−1
alternatives.note: 0.3-0.6 A/px conflicts with the 0.231-0.788 A/px of M08 Table 2

dispersion_per_order.note: M08 text: 'the order number is followed by the central wavelength of the order and the dispersion at that wavelength' (column 'Dlambda (Å)'; per pixel by the arithmetic below).
dispersion_per_order.derived: DERIVED: c x Dlambda/Lambda = 22.2 (order 20), 22.5 (17), 22.6 (15), 22.9 (11), 23.0 (9), 23.5 (8), 24.4 (6) km/s/px. Littrow with f_cam 138 mm and 13.5 um: c x 0.0135/(2 tan 32.3 x 138) = 23.2 km/s/px; Table 2 / Littrow = 0.955 (order 20) rising to 1.050 (order 6).

order_central_wavelengths.quote: The approximate central wavelenght for any order is equal to 6.2 micron/(order number).
order_central_wavelengths.note: [sic] 'wavelenght'. Compare M08 Table 2 central wavelengths: m x lambda = 62500 (order 20), 61950 (15), 61490 (11), 60160 (8), 58200 (6) A.
order_central_wavelengths.derived: DERIVED: Littrow blaze from the sourced constants 2 sin(32.3)/175 = 6.107 um -> lambda_b = 6107/m nm (order 11: 5552 A)

order_wavelength_ranges.note: Table as printed has inconsistencies: order 12 lambda_min 4286 is below order 13's 4469, and order 20 (3197-3311) lies inside order 19 (3187-3430). Use orders 6-11 and 13-19 with care.

wavelength_coverage.quote: The wavelength coverage includes the entire optical window (3100 Å - 1 µm).

alternatives.quote: full wavelength coverage of the visible spectrum (3200 Å – 1 µm)
The wavelength coverage of MagE is approximately 3100 Å to 1 micron.
instrument’s wavelength coverage spans 3000 - 10500 Å over 15 orders (6 < m < 20), continuous except for a 15 Å gap near 9500 Å between orders six and seven

spatial_scale.quote: the scale at the detector is 3 pixels per arcsec on the sky

alternatives.quote: The plate scale at the detector is 0.3 arcsec/pixel.
Each pixel subtends 0.33′′ on the sky.

spatial_scale.derived: DERIVED from optics: 206264.8/(71526.4 x 138/1094) x 0.0135 = 0.309 arcsec/px (3.24 px per arcsec)

image_quality.quote: The measured image diameter (using a 0.35 arcsec square entrance aperture) is less than 2.0 pixels FWHM everywhere in the field; the average image diameter is 1.8 pixels.
image_quality.derived: DERIVED: a 0.35" aperture projects to 1.13 px (0.35 x 3.24), so the optics add ~1.4 px FWHM in quadrature

sampling_1arcsec.quote: the scale at the detector is 3 pixels per arcsec on the sky
sampling_1arcsec.derived: DERIVED: 1" x 0.3468 mm x 138/1094 / 13.5 um = 3.24 px (no anamorphic factor applied: prism rotations NOT FOUND)

not_found: Echelle in-plane (theta) and out-of-plane (gamma) angles: only 'quasi-Littrow' (M08).
Prism rotation / incidence angles (M08 says they were 'adjusted to control the anamorphic beam distortion'); prism sizes; the order of the three prism passes is inferred, not stated.
Fused-silica grade of the prisms (use Malitson 1965).
Minimum order separation in arcsec or pixels (M08: orders separate 'when used with a 10 arcsec slit').
Which wavelength / order falls at the detector centre (needed for the app's central wavelength).
Default CCD binning; default slit (1.0" is only the reference slit for R).
Measured R for slits other than 1" and 2" (R18); the grating vendor / catalogue number.
The MagE section of the Magellan instrument web pages beyond the LCO manual (the URL given in M08, lco.cl/lco/telescopes-information/..., was not fetched).
conflicts: Blaze: M08 '32.3 deg (6.2 um first order Littrow blaze)' and LCOMG '6.2 micron' vs 2 sin(32.3 deg)/175 = 6.107 um (DERIVED, -1.5%); 6.2 um would need delta = 32.85 deg. The M08 Table 2 central wavelengths give m x lambda = 61,200-62,500 A for orders 9-20 (6.2 um fits these better), 58,200 for order 6.

Resolution at 1": R = 4100 (M08, LCOMG, MGHO; design) vs 4770 +/- 8 measured from sky lines (R18); at 2": 2545 +/- 37 measured vs ~2000 geometric (DERIVED). R18 calls the measured values 'higher than the design resolution'.
Slit count: eight widths (M08, LCOMG, MGHO) vs 'Five non-overlapping slits' (B09).
Spatial scale: 0.3"/px (M08, LCOMG, MGHO) vs 0.33" (B09) vs 0.309" DERIVED from 1094/138 mm and f/11.
Dispersion: 0.231-0.788 A/px (M08 Table 2) vs '0.3 A/px (blue) to 0.6 A/px' (B09); B09 '22 km/s per pixel' is the blue end of the DERIVED 22.2-24.4 km/s/px.
Coverage: 3100 A - 1 um (M08 abstract, LCOMG) vs 3200 A - 1 um (M08 Sec. 1; MGHO 3200-10000) vs 3000-10500 A with a 15 A gap near 9500 A (B09).

Telescope: Clay folded port (M08 2008, B09 2009; R18: 'The majority of observations were conducted with MagE mounted on the Clay telescope') vs Baade folded port (MGHO 2017) / Baade AUX3 (LCOMG 2024).
Collimated beam: 99 mm (M08 Sec. 2) vs '~100 mm' (M08 Sec. 1) vs 99.45 mm DERIVED (1094/11.0).
B09 Table 2 order ranges are internally inconsistent (order 12 lambda_min 4286 < order 13 lambda_min 4469; order 20 inside order 19).
Flexure with elevation: 'at most 0.8 pixels' (M08 Sec. 5.2) vs 'about 0.1 pixels' (LCOMG) -- not used by the app.
notes: M08 states the optical design 'is very similar to the ESI spectrograph (Sheinis et al. 2002)': same 175 gr/mm, 32.3 deg echellette, reflective collimator, two prisms (one double-pass). MagE is ESI scaled to a 99 mm beam on an f/11 telescope with a 138 mm f/1.4 Schmidt camera.

Format check (DERIVED): Littrow dispersion with f_cam = 138 mm, 13.5 um pixels: 23.2 km/s/px; order 6 FSR (1617 A) spans ~2050 px at the tabulated 0.788 A/px -> the 2048-px axis is the dispersion axis and the reddest order just fills it (B09 notes a 15 A gap near 9500 A between orders 6 and 7).

The 1094 mm collimator at f/11.0 and the 138 mm camera reproduce the published 0.3"/px (0.309 DERIVED) and the 3-px-per-arcsec slit sampling, so R(1") ~ 4000 is a slit-width (geometric) prediction; the measured 4770 (R18) is 16% higher.
Throughput (M08 Table 2 / LCOMG): peak 21.8% (telescope + instrument) at 5590 A; 'Efficiency (instrument)' 35.5% -- not used by the app.
Wavelength calibration: ThAr, 'Typical wavelength solutions give an RMS of 0.06 A for 500 arc lines' (M08 Sec. 3.5).

esi.title: Keck II / ESI (Echellette Spectrograph and Imager, echellette mode: Cassegrain, two BSL7Y prisms, one in double pass)
esi.recommended_preset: 1.0" x 20" slit (R = 4000, 6.49 px; KECH Table 2). D = 10.95 m, F = 13.7 (project Keck convention; the ESI design report UCR96 says 'f/13.7 secondary' and '1.38 arc-sec/mm'; Keck pages say f/15, 0.725 mm/arcsec), 1 object, mirror collimator (off-axis paraboloid; S99 says off-axis segment of an ellipsoid) f_col = 2286 mm, W = 2286/13.7 = 166.9 mm (= UCR96's 6.57 in tip-to-tip beam; S02 quotes ~160 mm), camera: refractive 10-element all-spherical Epps camera, f = 308 mm (287 mm aperture, 'underfilled f/1.07'), echellette 175 l/mm (175.555 in UCR96), delta = 32.3 deg, 'nearly in Littrow' / quasi-Littrow with the incoming beam out of the dispersion plane by 'a few degrees' (numeric gamma NOT FOUND: theta = 0, gamma = 0 here), orders 6-15; cross-disperser: two 50 deg Ohara BSL7Y prisms, the first in double pass (before and after the grating) and the second in single pass = three passes, near minimum deviation (UCR96); BSL7Y Sellmeier from the OHARA data sheet (glass section below; N-BK7 is within 0.3-1.2% in dn/dlambda over 0.4-1.0 um, DERIVED); detector MIT/LL CCID20 4096 (dispersion, DERIVED) x 2048 x 15 um (default binning NOT stated; Keck advises full-frame readout). Validate against the per-order wavelength solutions (KQR: 0.1545 A/px at 4077 A in order 15 ... 0.3345 A/px at 8708 A in order 7 = 11.34-11.52 km/s/px DERIVED; '11.4 km/s/pixel' average S02, 'constant 11.5' KECH), the free spectral ranges per order (KECH Table 1: order 6 9366-11068 A ... order 15 3927-4198 A), coverage 3900-11000 A, the measured scale along the slit 0.120"/px (order 15) to 0.168"/px (order 6) (KQR) and 0.1542"/px in imaging, and R vs slit (KECH Table 2: 0.3" 13,400; 0.5" 8000; 0.75" 5400; 1.0" 4000; 1.25" 3200; 6" 700 -- slit width x 11.5 km/s/px, i.e. geometric). Central wavelength: the chip centre in the cross-dispersion direction falls between orders 11 and 12 at about 5250 A (DERIVED from the UCR96 order heights).

Prism glass: Ohara BSL7Y (S02, S99; as built) vs UBK7 / 'UBK7/BK7Y (blue transmitting BK7)' (UCR96, design).

Dispersion: average 11.4 km/s/px and range 9.6-12.8 (S02) vs 'constant 11.5' (KECH) vs 11.34-11.52 from the KQR polynomials (DERIVED) vs 15 km/s/px (KTG02 specification).

Coverage upper limit: 1.09 um (S02) vs 10900 A (KOV) vs 1.1 um (KESP) vs order-6 FSR to 11068 A (KECH).
Scale along the slit per order: predicted 0.127-0.183"/px (S02 Table 1) vs measured 0.120-0.168"/px (KQR, KECH).
Minimum order separation: 22.0" (S02) vs 23.0" (UCR96 design table).
Detector scale: 0.1542 +/- 0.0010 (KESP) vs 0.153 (S02) vs 0.15 (KTG02) vs 0.1535 DERIVED.
notes: Consistency check (DERIVED): f_col 2286 mm, f_cam 308 mm, 0.725 mm/arcsec and 15 um pixels give 0.1535"/px (published 0.1542, 0.153); the Littrow dispersion 11.55 km/s/px agrees with the KQR per-order solutions to 0.3-1.8%; the Littrow FSR lengths reproduce UCR96's 'Width (%)' of the chip to 1-2 points.

Prism glass: the OHARA BSL7Y Sellmeier reproduces its data-sheet indices to <= 5e-6 from 0.326 to 1.129 um (DERIVED). N-BK7 (on the app list) is 4.7e-4 higher in n and within 0.3% (0.4-0.6 um) to 1.2% (1.0 um) in dn/dlambda, so an N-BK7 stand-in changes the cross-dispersion by about 1% (DERIVED).
MagE (M08) is described as 'very similar to the ESI spectrograph': same 175 gr/mm, 32.3 deg echellette and two-prism (one double-pass) layout.
ESI also has a low-dispersion (prism-only) mode and a direct-imaging mode (S02); only the echellette mode is relevant here.
UCR96 is a January 1996 design document (version 1.0): where it differs from S02 / the Keck pages, the later sources describe the as-built instrument.

Sellmeier_OHARA.form: n^2 - 1 = A1 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - B1) + A2 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - B2) + A3 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - B3)
Sellmeier_OHARA.wavelength_unit: um (B in um^2); 365-2325 nm to about +/-5e-6 (the page text layer prints the exponent as '×106'), limited to the tabulated range when a data sheet lists fewer indices
Sellmeier_OHARA.quote: By using this formula, refractive indices for any wavelength between 365 and 2325nm can be calculated to have an accuracy of around ± 5 ×106. ... When calculating a respective refractive index, please bear in mind that each wavelength is expressed in µm units.

used_in: ESI cross-disperser (two 50 deg prisms, first in double pass)
OHARA_BSL7Y.loc: BSL7Y data sheet, 'Constants of Dispersion Formula' (footer 'Date 10/2018')
OHARA_BSL7Y.note: S02/S99 name 'Ohara BSL7Y' (UCR96 design: 'UBK7/BK7Y (blue transmitting BK7)'). Coefficients printed with decimal commas. They reproduce the sheet's indices to <= 5e-6 over 0.326-1.129 um, but deviate by -2.3e-5 at 1.530 um, -1.4e-4 at 1.970 um and -3.6e-4 at 2.325 um (DERIVED) -- use only to 1.13 um (ESI works at 0.39-1.1 um). No validity range is printed on this sheet.

checks: BSL7Y (OHI): coefficients reproduce the data-sheet indices nd 1.51633, ne 1.51825, nF 1.52189, nC 1.51386, ng 1.52619, nh 1.52973, ni 1.53574, n(326.1) 1.54422, n(1013.98) 1.50681, n(1128.64) 1.50528 to <= 5e-6; beyond 1.5 um the residual grows to -3.6e-4 (2.325 um).

N-BK7 (round-1 SCHOTT coefficients) vs BSL7Y (DERIVED): n higher by 4.7e-4 (0.5-0.8 um) to 5.3e-4 (0.365 um); dn/dlambda ratio N-BK7/BSL7Y = 1.0032 (0.4 um), 1.0030 (0.5), 1.0015 (0.6), 0.9961 (0.8), 0.9883 (1.0 um).
MagE prisms are fused silica (M08): use the round-1 Malitson 1965 formula already in the app; grade not stated.
